name: ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Ltd
title: ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Ltd - 544658 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Asset manager with market share steady at 13.4% and equity share 14%; growth is mark-to-market led, SIP flows flat QoQ at ~INR 31,781 cr in June, and no supply-side capacity signals since AMCs have no capex cycle.

triggers.label: SIP rebound in June vs May
triggers.quote: June 2026 recorded SIP contribution of INR 31,781 crores.

triggers.label: Debt AUM down 6% QoQ
triggers.quote: resulting in a sequential moderation of 6% in quarterly average AUM

red_flags.label: Other income swing from MTM
red_flags.quote: Other income of INR181 crores turned positive from negative vis-a-vis last quarter on the back of positive mark-to-market.

evasions.topic: SIP breakup by scheme and ticket size
evasions.quote: We haven't given the breakup across the asset or across the schemes.
We'll come back to you on the number separately
So we don't give guidance for future

summary.headline: ICICI Pru AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 23.1% YoY to INR965 crore on 18.3% YoY MF AUM growth and a mark-to-market gain in other income.
summary.overview: Quarter-average mutual fund AUM reached INR11.17 lakh crore, up 1.1% QoQ and 18.3% YoY, with market share of 13.4% and second-place ranking. Operating revenue rose 17.6% YoY to INR1,564 crore, and other income swung to INR181 crore positive on June-end mark-to-market gains. Operating expenses rose 14.3% QoQ, mainly from employee costs, with ESOP charges now debited for the first time. Operating PBT was INR1,100 crore (+20.2% YoY) and PAT INR965 crore (+23.1% YoY). Industry SIP flows were flat-to-soft in the quarter and June rebounded, while the company said its own numbers track the industry.

financial_highlights.change: Positive vs negative in previous quarter, on mark-to-market

segments.name: Mutual fund
segments.commentary: Share of operating net revenue 90.02%; market share 13.4% overall, 13.5% in active schemes (INR9.25 lakh crore), 14% in equity (INR6.31 lakh crore). Equity-oriented hybrid QAAUM INR2.22 lakh crore, 26.6% share.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, AIF, private credit, real estate, PE, offshore advisory)
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR79,446 crore; PMS INR28,996 crore (+8.1% QoQ); AIF INR22,737 crore. Share of operating net revenue 8.54%.

segments.name: Advisory
segments.commentary: Share of operating net revenue 1.44%; yield on assets under advisory 30 bps. AUM moderated on international redemptions, per management.

segments.name: SIF (iSIF)
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR2,678 crore; four of seven permitted strategies launched, two of them in June 2026.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; it pointed to the June-quarter employee cost as the run-rate base.
ESOP cost for FY27 indicated at INR64-68 crore, charged evenly across quarters.
No negative impact from TER regulation changes; the company said it passed the change through to distributors.
Management said several product launches are planned over the next nine months, including life-cycle funds, a contra fund, ETFs, a SIF sector rotation strategy and commercial real estate AIFs.
capex_capacity: Presence in more than 300 towns; new office openings are decided at regional level each year.
Four iSIF strategies live and three permitted strategies still pending, with one more approval in hand (sector rotation SIF).
GIFT City: one inbound fund (ICICI Prudential Smart Navigator Fund) live; more inbound and outbound products under evaluation.
Investment book: about 50% is seed capital, largely marked to market under the SEBI formula; the AIF/other equity/REIT share of the investment book is 23.5% and its MTM exposure was not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM INR83.28 lakh crore, +15.4% YoY and +2% QoQ; closing AUM +11.6% QoQ. Equity AUM INR45.2 lakh crore.
Industry equity net flows INR1.14 lakh crore, down INR10,064 crore QoQ; June flows rebounded 26% MoM. June SIP contribution INR31,781 crore, roughly flat QoQ.
Company systematic transactions (SIP plus STP) were INR4,872 crore in June vs INR5,104 crore in March 2026.
Debt QAAUM down 6% QoQ to INR11.93 lakh crore on institutional redemptions amid tight corporate liquidity.
Equity distribution mix: MFDs 36.2%, national distributors 15.9%, ICICI Bank 7.7%, other banks 10.7%, direct 29.5%.
Margins (annualised): equity 66 bps, debt 32 bps, liquid 12 bps, passive 12 bps, arbitrage 30 bps. Alternates net yield 95 bps, which management said normally runs 90-100 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% PAT growth and what helped in Q1 despite geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited resilient industry net flows and SIP over the prior year. Net sales were over INR4.6 lakh crore in FY26, and mark-to-market gains on the equity base also lifted PAT.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the change in market share, flows vs MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly share shifts are mainly MTM-driven given the high equity AUM base. Small caps returned 24%, mid caps 17.2% and large caps 8.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP cost and how should employee opex be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 ESOP cost is INR64-68 crore, charged evenly (not front-loaded). Management said the June quarter's INR200 crore quarterly opex is a fair base for modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP flows fall and what is the ticket-size or stoppage picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the net SIP trigger fell because stoppages of older SIPs exceeded new SIP registrations. It said count does not matter and only the net effect is shown. It did not split SIP by ticket size or scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt AUM fall in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to institutional redemptions as corporates used liquidity for working capital during the war-related disruption, not to seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for alternates net yield and new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Net yield typically runs 90-100 bps depending on product mix. Life-cycle MF funds follow SEBI's predefined expense structure and start equity-heavy, then shift to debt nearer maturity.

qa_highlights.question: Is staff cost going to moderate after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is the run rate. Compensation changes take effect from 1 April, with employee costs up 11% YoY. QoQ growth was partly due to reversals in Q4 FY26 and to campus hiring in Q1.

risks_watch: SIP trigger and June SIP run-rate (INR31,781 crore industry; company SIP+STP INR4,872 crore in June) as the next test of retail flow stickiness.
Debt AUM outflows from institutional and corporate liquidity; mix of debt AUM is a watch item.
MTM sensitivity: about 50% of the investment book is seed capital, so the other income line swings with markets (INR181 crore this quarter vs negative in Q4 FY26).
Alternates yield and mix shifts; PMS/AIF net yield of 95 bps with fees and commissions rising in line with volumes.
Employee costs and ESOP run-rate are now in the P&L; opex growth could stay elevated versus prior-year levels.
SIF category is early-stage; management said distribution is still limited and advisor participation needs to grow.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the franchise and long-term flows, but guarded on near-term SIP and debt trends, which management repeatedly said should be read quarterly rather than monthly. Management was evasive on the SIP ticket-size breakdown, the MTM share of alternates and the 23.5% investment-book split, and gave no formal guidance.

growth.why: No formal guidance; management cited several product launches over nine months (life-cycle funds, contra fund, ETFs, SIF sector rotation, commercial real estate AIFs) with no capacity or timing numbers, and ESOP cost guided at INR64-68 crore for FY27.
